item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 221136
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 AM EDT Thu Oct 22 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Subtropical
Storm Josephine, located a few hundred miles offshore of the
Mid-Atlantic coast of the United States.

Subtropical Central Atlantic:
A trough of low pressure located several hundred miles to the
east-southeast of Bermuda is producing a large area of disorganized
showers and thunderstorms. Some development of this system is
possible during the next day or two while it moves slowly
north-northeastward. Upper-level winds are forecast to become too
strong for further development by the weekend.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...10 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Josephine are issued under WMO header WTNT35
KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPAT5.
Forecast/Advisories on Josephine are issued under WMO header WTNT25
KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMAT5.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Subtropical Storm Josephine Public Advisory Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM AST Thu Oct 22 2026 
000
WTNT35 KNHC 221435
TCPAT5
 
BULLETIN
Subtropical Storm Josephine Advisory Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL102026
1100 AM AST Thu Oct 22 2026
 
...JOSEPHINE MOVING NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE NORTHWESTERN 
ATLANTIC...
...EXPECTED TO BECOME A POWERFUL EXTRATROPICAL CYCLONE THIS
AFTERNOON OR TONIGHT...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM AST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...39.2N 67.3W
ABOUT 200 MI...320 KM SE OF NANTUCKET MASSACHUSETTS
ABOUT 420 MI...675 KM SSW OF HALIFAX NOVA SCOTIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NE OR 45 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM AST (1500 UTC), the center of Subtropical Storm Josephine
was located near latitude 39.2 North, longitude 67.3 West. The storm
is moving toward the northeast near 12 mph (19 km/h), and this
motion, along with an increase in forward speed, is expected to
continue into tonight. A gradual turn toward the east is forecast on
Friday and into the weekend. On the forecast track, Josephine should
move away from the United States and remain south of Nova Scotia and
Newfoundland during the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Some additional strengthening is forecast through the day
today while Josephine begins to transition to an extratropical
cyclone. Josephine is expected to become a powerful extratropical
cyclone with hurricane-force winds tonight or early Friday.
 
Winds of 40 mph extend outward up to 415 miles (665 km) from the
center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
WIND: Gale-force winds are possible in gusts along portions of the
northeastern United States coast through today. See products issued
by your local National Weather Service office for more details.
 
COASTAL FLOODING: Minor to locally moderate coastal flooding is
ongoing along portions of the U.S. Mid-Atlantic coast and will
continue through the rest of the week around times of high tide.
Please refer to products issued by your local National Weather
Service forecast office for more information.
 
SURF: Large swells generated by Josephine are affecting much of the
eastern seaboard of the United States and portions of Atlantic
Canada. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and
rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office.
 
A depiction of rip current risk for the United States can be found
at: hurricanes.gov/graphics_at5.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM AST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Subtropical Storm Josephine Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM AST Thu Oct 22 2026 
ZCZC MIATCDAT5 ALL
TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
 
Subtropical Storm Josephine Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL102026
1100 AM AST Thu Oct 22 2026

Satellite imagery this morning indicates that an area of convection 
has developed to the north of the center of Josephine, although the 
convective curvature is less than it was last night.  Just- received 
scatterometer data suggests the convective cluster is near or just 
west of a developing frontal boundary. Satellite intensity estimates 
have changed little since the previous advisory, and the 
scatterometer shows winds near 50 kt west of the center. The initial 
intensity remains 55 kt based on a subtropical cyclone intensity 
estimate from TAFB and the possibility of the scatterometer 
undersampling the maximum wind.

The initial motion is northeastward or 040/10 kt.  GOES RGB airmass 
imagery shows a mid- to upper-level trough extending from eastern 
Canada southwestward into the northeastern US, and Josephine should 
accelerate northeastward during the next 12-24 h as this trough 
amplifies and approaches the cyclone. After 24 h or so, Josephine 
should turn more eastward as it becomes embedded in the mid- 
latitude westerlies. On the forecast track, the center of Josephine 
will move away from the New England states today and pass south of 
Nova Scotia and Newfoundland tonight and Saturday. The guidance is 
again tightly clustered, and the new forecast track is similar to 
the previous forecast.

The interaction between Josephine and the aforementioned trough 
should cause the cyclone to develop fronts and become extratropical 
during the next 12 h, and the scatterometer data suggests this 
process is already underway. However, intensification is expected 
during this transition and Josephine will become a hurricane-force 
extratropical low later tonight and on Friday. The dynamical models 
are in good agreement that the cyclone should steadily weaken after 
24 h, and they forecast Josephine to dissipate between 72 and 96 h 
as it is absorbed by a new low pressure area developing to its 
northeast. The new intensity forecast is based mainly on the global 
physical models and it has only minor adjustments from the last 
forecast.  The wind radii forecasts have also been revised based on 
the global model forecasts.
 
Since the coastal wind hazards associated with this system have been
covered for the last several days through non-tropical products
issued by local National Weather Service offices, those products
will remain in effect until the threat diminishes and Josephine
moves farther away from the U.S. coast over the next day or so.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
